findings.evidence: The baseline registry audit contained 82 advisory records and 83 vulnerability instances (12 critical, 37 high, 27 moderate, 7 low) across 25 package groups.
findings.correction: Upgraded Orval, Vite, Zod and compatible form resolvers; applied patched releases within existing major lines for remaining transitive packages. Retained pnpm 10.26.1 and minimumReleaseAge=1440. Regenerated the trusted API client with explicit React Query v5 configuration.
findings.reason: Critical Orval findings concern code generation with hostile API specifications; they do not establish remote execution through the static patient site. Express/proxy and build dependencies also require remediation. Newest releases were not accepted when younger than the one-day safeguard.
findings.validation: The post-remediation registry audit reports zero known advisories; full build, generator and typechecks pass. Every original advisory and affected dependency path is retained in dependency-advisories.json.

findings.evidence: JSON null and numeric firstName threw TypeError in Pages/Workers; a numeric name caused Express HTTP 500. An address such as bad@ reached the mock provider.
findings.correction: Validate unknown input as a non-null object; normalize and bound email; validate optional names and a deduplicated interest allowlist.
findings.reason: TypeScript annotations do not validate incoming JSON. Bad inputs must receive controlled client errors before reaching a paid external service.
findings.validation: All three adapters reject invalid types, malformed JSON, unsupported interests and malformed email with HTTP 400 and zero provider calls.

findings.issue: Unbounded edge request bodies and names
findings.evidence: Pages/Workers accepted a 20,000-character name; the Express default parser also accepted it. Edge handlers read the entire body without a project limit.
findings.correction: Apply a 4 KiB byte limit, including streams without Content-Length; limit names to 100 characters; require uncompressed application/json. Express uses a small raw parser with inflation disabled.
findings.reason: Limits reduce memory/provider abuse and avoid relying on attacker-controlled Content-Length.
findings.validation: Oversized bodies return 413; oversized names return 400; text/plain/compressed payloads return 415; no provider request is made.

findings.status: Corrected in source; bot abuse remains open
findings.issue: Cross-origin signup and permissive Express CORS
findings.evidence: Both edge handlers accepted foreign-Origin simple text/plain requests, which browsers can send without a JSON preflight. Express advertised Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.
findings.correction: Reject foreign/opaque origins and cross-site Fetch Metadata; remove blanket CORS and unused form decoding. Edge compares origins; Express compares host for HTTPS-proxy compatibility without trusting arbitrary forwarded headers.
findings.reason: Prevent opportunistic browser cross-site submission. This does not authenticate clients or stop bots that omit/spoof browser headers.
findings.validation: Foreign/opaque Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site cases return 403 across all adapters; responses no longer advertise wildcard CORS.

findings.evidence: Every backend sent status=subscribed for a supplied email address.
findings.correction: Send status=pending for new subscribers; update success copy and draft privacy explanation to describe email confirmation.
findings.reason: Someone should not be automatically subscribed just because another visitor supplies their address. This is a deliberate backend behavior change requiring deployment review.
findings.validation: Mock-provider assertions verify pending in all runtimes. No real address was subscribed and no confirmation email was sent; actual audience settings and delivery remain unverified.

findings.evidence: The API returned Subscribed successfully versus Already subscribed, revealing whether an address was already on the list.
findings.correction: Return identical status and message for successful new requests and Member Exists. Do not expose provider error detail.
findings.reason: Reduce list-membership disclosure, especially for a health-related audience. This is not a constant-time/non-enumeration guarantee against every provider behavior.
findings.validation: Regression cases compare successful/new and existing-member JSON exactly and verify private provider errors do not appear in responses.

findings.evidence: Baseline provider requests had no AbortSignal; the UI also had no deadline.
findings.correction: Use an eight-second provider deadline and a twelve-second browser deadline with recoverable error copy.
findings.reason: A stalled provider should not hold the visitor or backend indefinitely.
findings.validation: Each adapter passes an abort-aware mock-provider timeout case and returns controlled 502.

findings.status: Corrected in source; historical retention unverified
findings.evidence: Express explicitly logged email addresses and provider error payloads for success, existing membership and errors.
findings.correction: Remove newsletter PII/provider-payload logging; retain minimal request method/path/status logging.
findings.reason: Email addresses and audience preferences should not enter routine operational logs unnecessarily.
findings.validation: Source review confirms the shared provider handler does not log subscriber input or provider bodies. Existing provider/host logs and deletion/retention cannot be inspected from this session.

findings.evidence: Pages, Workers and Express independently implemented the same provider flow; only some had particular checks.
findings.correction: Use one runtime-neutral contract with small adapters and official Cloudflare edge typechecking.
findings.reason: A security correction should apply to every supported deployment path and remain testable.
findings.validation: The same regression cases execute through all three adapters; the edge and Express TypeScript gates pass.

findings.status: Configured in source; live enforcement unverified
findings.evidence: The repository had no _headers/security-response configuration. This is a source finding, not proof that Cloudflare currently lacks account-level headers.
findings.correction: Add Cloudflare static CSP, framing protection, nosniff, referrer and permissions policies, and host-only HSTS. Add dynamic JSON headers. Emit a production-only meta CSP subset for static mirrors.
findings.reason: Constrain script/object/frame execution and reduce unnecessary disclosure. Inline styles remain allowed for React/motion/Leaflet; inline scripts are not allowed. HSTS intentionally has no preload/includeSubDomains.
findings.validation: A real Chromium test blocks an injected inline script; the local simulated header server exercises checked-in policy. GitHub Pages cannot provide all arbitrary response headers from _headers. Production enforcement is not verified.

findings.evidence: Throwing SecurityError from localStorage.getItem removed the main page; saved search history {} caused .filter is not a function when selecting a result.
findings.correction: Guard storage reads/writes; validate history as an array of current known search records, deduplicate and cap it; allow nonpersistent banner dismissal.
findings.reason: Storage is optional and untrusted. Browsing a patient information site should not depend on it being available or correctly shaped.
findings.validation: Browser tests with corrupt history and denied reads/writes successfully navigate to the oxygen article with no runtime errors.

findings.evidence: GitHub Pages has no newsletter POST service, but its footer offered a form targeting /api/newsletter/subscribe outside the repository base.
findings.correction: Do not render or collect newsletter fields on repository-subpath builds; show clear unavailability text. Root builds preserve the integration, with an optional VITE_NEWSLETTER_ENABLED=false switch.
findings.reason: Avoid inviting visitors to submit personal information to an unavailable endpoint. A future subpath backend needs explicit configuration rather than assumption.
findings.validation: Subpath browser checks show no newsletter email field and no signup request. Cloudflare-compatible root builds retain the form.

findings.issue: Generic titles and incomplete static route heads
findings.evidence: Most pages kept the generic document title; only four involvement pages had crawler-readable route files. GitHub direct arrivals otherwise relied on its 404 fallback.
findings.correction: Use the shared route index for browser title/description updates and generate all 35 canonical HTML entry pages. Correct resource metadata to describe unavailable drafts. Preserve origin validation and optional canonical/image tags.
findings.reason: Titles orient visitors/assistive technology; static route files give crawlers and direct arrivals useful page-specific heads without guessing the permanent origin.
findings.validation: 35-route artifact tests pass; four representative subpath direct arrivals return 200 locally with correct assets; configured test origin/base tags and rejected unsafe origins are checked.

findings.issue: Inactive clinical controls resemble working links
findings.evidence: The professional page showed a referral button without a handler and guideline cards styled as clickable without destinations.
findings.correction: Replace these controls with explicit in-development/review-pending text, removing misleading pointer/link decoration.
findings.reason: Do not imply that clinical referral guidance has been published or verified when no destination exists.
findings.validation: Source and browser review confirm honest pending labels. The user-required For Healthcare Professionals utility button remains.

findings.status: Corrected in source; repository settings unverified
findings.issue: Workflow privilege and mutable action references
findings.evidence: CI omitted explicit token permissions; Pages build inherited deployment write/token privileges. Actions referenced movable major tags.
findings.correction: Set CI read-only permissions; give only the Pages deploy job pages/id-token write; disable persisted checkout credentials; pin top-level actions to verified commit hashes; add weekly dependency/action update PRs and audit/type/runtime checks.
findings.reason: Reduce exposure if build/dependency code is compromised and keep patches visible. Action pins do not pin every internal dependency of each action.
findings.validation: Workflow configuration and immutable hashes cross-checked against GitHub tag refs; matching local commands pass. Required reviews, protection rules and account settings are separate verification gaps.

findings.evidence: No tracked .env/credential file was found, but .gitignore did not exclude environment files or Cloudflare local secret files.
findings.correction: Ignore .env variants, .dev.vars variants and audit scratch files while permitting named example templates.
findings.reason: Reduce accidental future credential commits; ignore rules do not remove historical secrets.
findings.validation: Tracked-file review and redacted history/artifact scans found no confirmed credential.

findings.evidence: Both Vite configurations set allowedHosts=true while listening on all interfaces.
findings.correction: Restore default hostname protection; permit only an explicitly configured REPLIT_DEV_DOMAIN for development; remove preview allow-all. Add actual Vite-config/build-plugin typechecks.
findings.reason: Restrict DNS-rebinding exposure when developers run local or hosted preview servers. This is not evidence that the static production host is vulnerable.
findings.validation: Development renders without runtime errors; Host localhost returns 200 and Host untrusted.example returns 403 in the local Vite check.

findings.evidence: Generated worksheet PDF included emergency/navigation bars and newsletter/footer UI, wasting space and interrupting the worksheet.
findings.correction: Hide site chrome and dialogs in print media while retaining article/worksheet content and the intended print heading.
findings.reason: Printed appointment preparation should remain readable and useful without screen-only controls.
findings.validation: Regenerated print PDF and browser print assertions confirm hidden header/footer and one visible heading in each medium.

findings.issue: Failed article chunk leaves blank site
findings.evidence: Blocking the travel/oxygen JavaScript chunk removed the entire main page with no recovery control.
findings.correction: Wrap article loading in a route-resetting error boundary with an accessible explanation/reload control; retain navigation.
findings.reason: A temporary asset/network failure should leave visitors able to recover or choose another section.
findings.validation: With a simulated 503 for that chunk, the recovery button appears and the professional navigation successfully opens another page.

findings.evidence: Axe WCAG 2.2 target-size findings reproduce at mobile and desktop widths where nearby centre markers overlap.
findings.correction: No marker redesign in this audit. Preserve searchable keyboard-operable centre list; plan clustering/expansion or a list-first map redesign and touch/assistive-technology review.
findings.reason: Hiding markers from the audit or removing keyboard operation would not resolve the usability problem. The list mitigates access but does not establish map conformance.
findings.validation: Remains the only settled-page automated accessibility rule violation across the 70 views. Full manual accessibility certification is not claimed.

findings.issue: No verified durable signup abuse control
findings.evidence: Source has no durable throttling/challenge and account-level WAF/rate rules are not visible. Origin checks can be omitted/spoofed by a bot. Double opt-in can still generate unsolicited confirmation emails.
findings.correction: Before promoting signup, configure and verify an edge/durable limit and, if appropriate, an accessible challenge, with provider quotas/alerts and documented owner. Do not add an unreliable in-memory Worker counter.
findings.reason: One instance-local counter does not enforce limits across isolates; inventing a binding or claiming an unseen WAF exists would be misleading.
findings.validation: Acceptance: repeated synthetic requests receive controlled 429/challenge before reaching a mocked provider; legitimate/shared-network users and recovery behavior pass review. Not executable without hosting configuration.

findings.evidence: The root build still emits a JavaScript chunk above Vite’s 500 kB uncompressed warning threshold. The full public output also contains downloadable brand assets.
findings.correction: Keep the warning visible; separately profile real devices and split dependencies only where measurement supports it. No warning-threshold suppression.
findings.reason: Total public build bytes are not the same as the initial page download; bundle warnings alone do not prove a poor real-user performance score.
findings.validation: Root/subpath production builds pass; no public source maps. Real network/Core Web Vitals testing remains outstanding.

findings.issue: Australian urgent-support numbers presented to ANZ audience
findings.evidence: The shared emergency banner displays Australian 000/Lifeline/Beyond Blue numbers without a clear Australian territorial label, while the site targets Australia and New Zealand.
findings.correction: Flag for a verified country-specific urgent-support review by the content/clinical owner before wider ANZ distribution. Do not silently infer or publish unreviewed replacement service details.
findings.reason: Technical success is not clinical approval; emergency signposting must be relevant to the visitor’s jurisdiction.
findings.validation: The discrepancy is confirmed from source. Service currency, New Zealand alternatives, clinical articles and specialist-directory accuracy were not clinically validated in this audit.
